name: Synthetic Tabular Data in Health Evaluation Framework
description: The generation of synthetic tabular data has emerged as a key privacy-enhancing technology to address challenges in data sharing, particularly in healthcare, where sensitive attributes can compromise patient privacy. Despite significant progress, balancing fidelity, utility, and privacy in complex medical datasets remains a substantial challenge. This paper introduces a comprehensive and holistic evaluation framework for synthetic tabular data, consolidating metrics and privacy risk measures across three key categories (fidelity, utility and privacy) and incorporating a fidelity-utility tradeoff metric. The framework was applied to three open-source medical datasets to evaluate synthetic tabular data generated by five generative models, both with and without differential privacy. Results showed that simpler models generally achieved better fidelity and utility, while more complex models provided lower privacy risks.
